<reflection>
The first experiment shows nearly all mechanisms fit comparably well (NLL ~-22.6), indicating a single run at moderate conditions cannot discriminate. Slightly better fits for M3, M6, M8 suggest dimerization/activation effects might be at play, but differences are tiny. M9, M11, M20 fit slightly worse. The aim to get a baseline was achieved but discrimination remains poor.
</reflection>

<hypothesis>
To discriminate, I should vary catalyst concentration substantially. Mechanisms involving catalyst dimerization (M2, M3, M13, M18, M19) or activation equilibrium (M6, M8) predict non-linear rate dependence on [cat]. Deactivation mechanisms (M9-M20) depend on absolute catalyst loading and show time-dependent activity loss more prominently at low [cat]. Running at a much higher catalyst concentration would:
- Amplify dimerization effects (M2, M3, M13, M18, M19) - rate should scale sub-linearly with [cat]
- Enhance cat+catS inactivation pathways (M19)
- Show faster deactivation plateaus (M9, M13)
- Activation equilibria (M6, M8) would differ from simple MM (M1)

High catalyst concentration at 0.1 M (10x baseline) with same substrate should provide strong contrast.
</hypothesis>
